summary: Streaming chat sessions disconnect or stall mid-generation for some customers (SSE/WebSocket)
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report streaming chat connections (SSE and WebSocket) disconnecting or stalling in the middle of model generation. Errors observed include sudden EOF on the socket, 499/502 proxy errors, and client-side timeouts after ~30s of no frames.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of dedicated customers in us-east using rw-large-v2 and open-7b.
- Interrupts user-facing chat applications (partial messages or stalls).
- Causes increased retries and user-visible latency.

Environment:
- prod (us-east), dedicated capacity pools for affected customers.
- API path: /v1/chat/stream (SSE) and /v1/chat/ws (WebSocket).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a streaming chat session with a long generation (>400 tokens) against rw-large-v2 in us-east.
2) Observe stream initially delivers tokens then disconnects or pauses mid-generation after 20-40s in some sessions.
3) Re-issuing the request sometimes succeeds (non-deterministic).

Logs & error patterns:
- proxy logs: repeated upstream connection resets to serving-runtime; 502 returned by streaming-proxy for some requests.
- application logs: client reported "socket closed by server" and "recv timeout" messages.
- metrics: increase in per-token latency and 5xx spikes starting 2026-03-01 22:00 UTC.

Additional notes:
- Customers report higher incidence during traffic bursts and when requests hit certain serving nodes.
- Similar tickets: SUP-31897 and SUP-8421 suggest streaming proxy or runtime regressions in the last kernel rollout.

Observe token stream then unexpected disconnect or stall after 20-40s

comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer Acme AI reported repeated mid-generation disconnects starting 2026-03-01 22:15 UTC. Customer provided request IDs and a session replay. Marking as P1 and escalating to SRE.

2026-03-02 - Priya Nair (SRE): Noted spike in 502s from streaming-proxy around 22:00 UTC. Initial hypothesis: connection pool exhaustion or upstream resets when serving-runtime GC/compile events occur. Collecting pprof and proxy connection stats.

2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor (Eng - serving-runtime): Reproduced stall locally with long-sequence workload. Observed long-tail token latencies correlate with kernel selection fallback path after quantized-kernel OOMs. Opening PR to improve fallback stability (github.com/redwood-rp/server/pull/4521).

2026-03-03 - Support (to customer): Temporary workaround - disable streaming (use non-stream endpoint) or reduce max_tokens to <300. Also suggested retry logic on client-side with exponential backoff. Customer to confirm impact.
2026-03-04 - SRE: Rolling back recent runtime kernel change deployed 2026-03-01 21:50 UTC to canary subset. Early telemetry shows decrease in 502 rate for affected pool.

2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor (Eng): Continued investigation into streaming-proxy connection handling under bursty upstream reconnects. Plan: harden proxy reconnection and add backpressure to prevent upstream OOM fallback path.
2026-03-04 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed reduced incidence after rollback but reports occasional stalls during peak. Keeping ticket open; next update in 24h or when fix PR merges.
investigation_notes:
Timeline of events: kernel rollout 2026-03-01 21:50 UTC -> spike in per-token latency and 502s starting 22:00 UTC -> customers report streaming disconnects. Repro steps show long generations trigger fallback kernel path which induces high tail latency; streaming-proxy sees upstream resets when runtime briefly reinits KV cache/compiles. Metrics indicate connection churn and pool saturation on a subset of nodes.
Hypotheses: (1) Fallback kernel path causes stalls/pauses in token emission; (2) Streaming-proxy doesn't tolerate upstream transient disconnects and returns 502 instead of reconnecting; (3) Dedicated pool had a configuration (low keepalive or connection pool size) exposing the bug.
Data collected: proxy logs, runtime pprof, kernel OOM traces, per-node latency histograms, trace samples for failing requests. PR 4521 addresses more robust kernel fallback and reduces blocking during kernel selection. SRE rollback of kernel rollout reduced error rate.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds applied: (A) Rollback of kernel rollout on 2026-03-04 to canary subset reduced 502 rate and customer reports fewer disconnects. (B) Recommended customer-side workarounds: reduce max_tokens, disable streaming, implement client retry/backoff.
Fix plan: Merge PR github.com/redwood-rp/server/pull/4521 (improves fallback path and non-blocking kernel selection), harden streaming-proxy reconnection logic, and increase connection pool limits for affected dedicated pools. Staged rollout with canary and metrics guard (5xx/latency thresholds).
Next steps: (1) Complete PR code review and run integration tests (owner: Liam O'Connor). (2) SRE to apply proxy reconnection patch and increase pool size for affected clusters (owner: Priya Nair). (3) Monitor telemetry for 48h post-rollout; if stable, close ticket and notify customer.
Estimated ETA for full fix: 2026-03-07 assuming no regressions in canary.
